# scripts/mutation-exec.sh is the "go test -exec" program of the mutation step: it runs one test binary, records the exit
# code against the mutated file, and exits with the code of the test binary. The test binary here is a fake that prints
# BIN_OUT and exits with BIN_RC. The copy folder stands for the module copy of one gremlins worker, and the orig folder
# for the module root. The mutant is the one file that differs, found by comparing the package of the copy with the orig.
[!exec:diff] skip
[!exec:gofmt] skip
script mutation-exec.sh exec.sh
chmod 755 fake/bin
env MUTATION_ROOT=$WORK/orig

# With no variables the script only runs the test binary: the output and the exit code pass, and nothing is recorded.
env MUTATION_ROOT=
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=
cd copy/sub
env BIN_OUT='plain output\n'
env BIN_RC=0
exec sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
stdout '^plain output$'
cd $WORK
env MUTATION_ROOT=$WORK/orig

# A mutant that the tests do not kill: exit 0, recorded with the line of the changed file. The output passes unchanged.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-pass
cd copy/sub
env BIN_OUT='ok  \tpkg\t0.01s\n'
env BIN_RC=0
exec sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
stdout '^ok  \tpkg\t0\.01s$'
grep -count=1 '^sub/p\.go\t3\t11\t9\t0\t$' $WORK/exits-pass
! grep 'extra\.go' $WORK/exits-pass
cd $WORK

# A killed mutant: exit 1 and the first failing line. A line that starts with "--- FAIL" wins over the lines before it.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-fail
cd copy/sub
env BIN_OUT='=== RUN   TestX\nnoise\n--- FAIL: TestX (0.10s)\n    x_test.go:9: bad\nFAIL\n'
env BIN_RC=1
exitcode 1 sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
stdout '^--- FAIL: TestX \(0\.10s\)$'
grep -count=1 '^sub/p\.go\t3\t11\t9\t1\t--- FAIL: TestX \(0\.10s\)$' $WORK/exits-fail
cd $WORK

# A test binary that a signal ended: the shell reports 128 plus the signal number, the record holds it, and so does the exit code of the script.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-signal
cd copy/sub
env BIN_OUT=
env BIN_RC=137
exitcode 137 sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
grep -count=1 '^sub/p\.go\t3\t11\t9\t137\t' $WORK/exits-signal
cd $WORK

# A failure with none of the failure words gives the first line of its output, and a tab in it becomes a space.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-first
cd copy/sub
env BIN_OUT='setup\tfailed\nsecond line\n'
env BIN_RC=2
exitcode 2 sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
grep -count=1 '^sub/p\.go\t3\t11\t9\t2\tsetup failed$' $WORK/exits-first
cd $WORK

# A package at the module root has the path with no folder.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-root
cd copy
env BIN_OUT=
env BIN_RC=0
exec sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
grep -count=1 '^p\.go\t3\t11\t9\t0\t$' $WORK/exits-root
cd $WORK

# Gremlins writes the mutant with go/printer, which reformats the file: here the alignment of the comments of the struct
# changes, as a mutant file of the real printer can. The record names the mutated line and column, not the first reformatted
# line. The mutation is "x > 1" to "x >= 1": the token ">" is at column 11, so the byte before the change is column 11.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-format
cd copy/fmt
env BIN_OUT=
env BIN_RC=0
exec sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
grep -count=1 '^fmt/q\.go\t9\t13\t11\t0\t$' $WORK/exits-format
! grep '\t4\t' $WORK/exits-format
cd $WORK

# A mutation can change the spacing before its token: "A*B + C" with "+" changed to "*" is written "A * B * C". The record
# names the token, column 13, and not the first byte that differs, column 10.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-space
cd copy/space
env BIN_OUT=
env BIN_RC=0
exec sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
grep -count=1 '^space/s\.go\t5\t13\t11\t0\t$' $WORK/exits-space
! grep '\t10\t' $WORK/exits-space
cd $WORK

# A mutation that lengthens a line can move the comments of the lines above it, which gofmt aligns. The first line that differs
# is then a line that differs in white space only, and the record names the mutated line, 5, not the line above it, 4.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-align
cd copy/align
env BIN_OUT=
env BIN_RC=0
exec sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
grep -count=1 '^align/a\.go\t5\t10\t8\t0\t$' $WORK/exits-align
cd $WORK

# A late record names its own mutant. The wrapper reads the mutant before the test binary runs, and the copy of the worker
# can hold another mutant when the test binary ends. The fake test binary replaces the file of the copy, as gremlins does
# when it restores the file after a timeout. The record still names the mutant that was applied when the run began.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-late
cd copy/late
env BIN_OUT=
env BIN_RC=0
env BIN_REWRITE=r.go
env ORIG_R=$WORK/orig/late/r.go
exec sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
grep -count=1 '^late/r\.go\t3\t11\t9\t0\t$' $WORK/exits-late
env BIN_REWRITE=
cd $WORK

# A test run in the module itself, such as the coverage run of gremlins, differs from nothing and leaves no record.
env MUTATION_EXIT_LOG=$WORK/exits-none
cd orig/sub
exec sh $WORK/exec.sh $WORK/fake/bin
! exists $WORK/exits-none
cd $WORK

-- fake/bin --
#!/bin/sh
printf '%b' "$BIN_OUT"
[ -z "${BIN_REWRITE:-}" ] || cp "$ORIG_R" "$BIN_REWRITE"
exit "$BIN_RC"
-- orig/go.mod --
module example.com/r

go 1.27
-- orig/p.go --
package r

var X = 1 + 1
-- orig/sub/p.go --
package sub

var X = 1 + 1
-- orig/sub/p_test.go --
package sub
-- copy/go.mod --
module example.com/r

go 1.27
-- copy/p.go --
package r

var X = 1 - 1
-- copy/sub/p.go --
package sub

var X = 1 - 1
-- copy/sub/p_test.go --
package sub
-- orig/fmt/q.go --
package fmt

type T struct {
	A    int    // one
	Name string // two
}

func F(x int) bool {
	return x > 1
}
-- copy/fmt/q.go --
package fmt

type T struct {
	A int // one
	Name string // two
}

func F(x int) bool {
	return x >= 1
}
-- orig/space/s.go --
package space

var A, B, C = 1, 2, 3

var X = A*B + C
-- copy/space/s.go --
package space

var A, B, C = 1, 2, 3

var X = A * B * C
-- orig/align/a.go --
package align

var (
	A = true  // one
	B = 1 < 2 // two
)
-- copy/align/a.go --
package align

var (
	A = true   // one
	B = 1 <= 2 // two
)
-- orig/late/r.go --
package late

var X = 1 + 1
-- copy/late/r.go --
package late

var X = 1 - 1
-- copy/sub/extra.go --
package sub

var Y = 2 - 2
